subject: Dedicated silo pricing, SLA tiers & GPU pool sizing options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Asha Ramesh <asha@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated silo pricing, SLA tiers & GPU pool sizing options

Hi Asha — great demo earlier. Thanks for the time.

Per our conversation, I attached a pricing workbook and an SLA scenarios PDF that lays out three sensible configurations for Dedicated capacity with single-tenant (silo) isolation:

- Scenario A — Small pilot: 2×16-GPU pool, best-effort latency SLOs, 3-month reserved commit (minimal premium)
- Scenario B — Production baseline: 6×16-GPU pool, 99th%-ile latency SLO + 1000 concurrent streams, 12-month reserved commit (mid premium)
- Scenario C — High-throughput: custom GPU pool (scale to 12×A100-equivalents), 99.9th%-ile SLO, dedicated networking + extended audit retention (highest premium)

Key compliance asks I want to confirm we covered: customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key), per-tenant audit logging (retention options: 90/365/730 days), and data residency in US/EU. Pricing in the worksheet includes a single-tenant premium line (expressed as a % uplift over standard Dedicated SKU) and optional hourly onboarding/ops fee for isolation hardening.

Questions for you:
- Which scenario maps closest to Acme's expected steady-state throughput (rough numbers for concurrent streams or tokens/sec helps us size the pool)?
- Do you have a target commit length (12/24/36 months) and a discount threshold (for example, is 15% discount on list committed spend acceptable)?

Next steps: if you can share target throughput and intended commit length, we will produce a final quote and a redline-ready contract.

Attachments: RI_Dedicated_Pricing_Worksheet_v3.xlsx; SLA_Scenarios_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
v: +1 415 555 0142
redwood.com

From: Asha Ramesh <asha@acme-ai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated silo pricing, SLA tiers & GPU pool sizing options

Vivek — thanks for the follow-up and the materials. Quick clarifying items from our CTO and security team:

1) KMS: We need a canonical answer whether customer-managed KMS can be used for all at-rest artifacts (models, cache, logs). If yes, is it supported in the pilot?
2) Audit logging: we need immutable logs with 1-year retention by default (longer is fine but price-sensitive). Can logs be exported to our SIEM (we use Splunk Cloud)?
3) EU residency: Some of our traffic originates in EU; can traffic + persisted data be pinned to an EU region for the run?

Also — we are evaluating discounting aggressively. For a 12-month commit at the Scenario B level (6×16-GPU), would you be able to provide a blended SLO-backed price with a 20% discount vs list if we agree to a 12-month upfront commit?

If you can answer these, we can pull procurement in.

—Asha
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme AI
asha@acme-ai.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Asha Ramesh <asha@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated silo pricing, SLA tiers & GPU pool sizing options

Thanks Asha — answers inline below.

1) KMS: Yes — BYOK is supported across persisted artifacts (model weights, checkpoint cache, and long-term storage). For the pilot we can enable customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault depending on region. HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise contracts (we can flag that as an add-on).

2) Audit logging: We capture per-tenant request/response metadata and system-level events. Default retention in a Dedicated silo is 90 days; we offer 365 and 730-day retention tiers as paid options. Logs can be exported to Splunk via S3 Gateway + Splunk HTTP Event Collector — we have a standard integration we can enable. For immutable storage we can configure object-lock on the S3 bucket (if required).

3) EU residency: Yes — we can pin the deployment and persisted backups to an EU region. For full EU residency for in-flight traffic we recommend routing through our EU dedicated zone; this will factor into hosting cost and isolation premium.

Regarding pricing: for Scenario B (6×16-GPU pool, 12-month commit) — with a 12-month upfront commitment we can consider a blended 18–22% discount off list for the committed usage. The single-tenant premium varies by scope:
- Basic silo (networked isolation, per-tenant logs 90d): +15%
- Hardened silo (BYOK, 365d logs, HSM option, dedicated VPC connectors): +22%
- Full compliance bundle (365/730d immutable logs, EU pinned, HSM, SOC2+custom attestations): +28–33%

We can also waive the one-time isolation onboarding fee if you commit to 12 months and the deal size passes our internal threshold — will confirm after legal loop. I attached our SOC2 attestation and the pricing workbook with the blended numbers filled in for Scenario B.

If that looks feasible, I’ll pull Karthik in to draft the commercial terms and a pilot SOW.

Thanks,
Vivek

Attachments: SOC2_attestation_2025.pdf; RI_Dedicated_Pricing_Worksheet_v3.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Dedicated silo pricing, SLA tiers & GPU pool sizing options

Internal note — draft commercial posture for ACME:

- Offer: Scenario B baseline (6×16-GPU), 12-month upfront commit
- Pricing: blended 20% discount off list for committed spend (midpoint of Vivek's 18–22%)
- Single-tenant premium: +20% (cap at +22% if BYOK+365d retention required)
- Onboarding: one-time $45k isolation setup fee, waived if contract >= $1.2M ARR committed
- SLA credits: standard SLA (99.9% infra uptime) with financial credits tied to 99th/99.9th p99 latency SLOs — propose a 5% credit bucket for breach events as we negotiate final wording
- Procurement asks: include a clause for audit evidence delivery (quarterly logs export) and explicit KMS key rotation window SLA

Attaching proposed contract redlines we will send to ACME once Vivek confirms acceptance.

Attachments: contract_redlines_v2.docx

Karthik
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Asha Ramesh <asha@acme-ai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated silo pricing, SLA tiers & GPU pool sizing options

Vivek / Karthik — thanks for the clarity. We reviewed the options with procurement and security. We’re comfortable to proceed with a pilot scoped to Scenario B (6×16-GPU) with:

- 12-month commit, 20% blended discount (upfront payment preferred)
- Single-tenant premium set to +20% (BYOK and 365d logs required)
- Onboarding fee waived as total committed spend meets your threshold
- EU pinning: start US region first; EU pinning to be added in month 3 as part of the pilot expansion plan

Please send the SOW + commercial redlines and we’ll route to procurement. Also can you confirm an approximate timeline for enabling BYOK in the pilot (we need the key rotation window defined)?

Once we have a DocuSign draft we’ll aim to execute within business week.

—Asha

Attachments referenced: none in-thread (procurement will expect DocuSign link)
